statements.label: theo:sampling_theorem
statements.title: [bengio2021flow]
statements.scope_notes: CLOSED IN A 2026-09-19 (Core/SamplingGeneral.lean; audited by an agent that did not write it; sorry-free, clean under warningAsError, axioms within propext/Classical.choice/Quot.sound). `MFlow.sampling_theorem` states the theorem on an arbitrary measurable space. F_init, F_term and F*_out are finite measures, pi* is a Markov kernel, F_term != 0, and flow matching is an equality of measures, F_init + F*_out.bind pi* = F_term + F*_out. Every clause is stated: F_init(S) = F_term(S); E(tau) = sum_{n>=0} P(tau > n) <= F*_out(S)/F_init(S) + 1 in [0, inf]; P(tau > n) -> 0 and P(tau <= n) -> 1; the law of s_tau EQUALS F_term/F_term(S) as a measure (app:notation's reading of s_tau ~ F_term); and P(tau <= n, s_tau in A) -> F_term(A)/F_term(S) for every measurable A. WEAKENED, harmlessly: Polish is never used, and F*_out is any finite measure rather than f*_out nu_B with f*_out in L1(nu_B). Every such F*_out is a finite measure, and the background measure is never used. DISCLOSED MODELLING: (1) The sampler is the absorbing Markov kernel `chainKernel` on S x Bool. It stops at x with probability stop = 1 - min(dF*_out/dG, 1), where G = F_term + F*_out, and G-a.e. this is the paper's dF_term/dG (`stop_ae_eq`). Its time-n laws are identified with the occupation marginals (`chainLaw_eq`, `occ_eq_chainLaw`, `stopped_eq_chainLaw`). No path-space measure is built. By absorption every event in the statement is an event of one marginal, so nothing is lost. (2) The law of s_tau is `sampleLaw`, the setwise limit of P(tau <= n, s_tau in .), that is, P(tau < inf, s_tau in .). Together with P(tau <= n) -> 1 it is the law of s_tau. (3) Off the support of G the stopping version is immaterial, because the occupation is <= G/Z (`occupation_le`). The bound is a domination, not an equality: Core/Sampling's `Parked.strict` shows it can be strict. INHABITED: `Resample.inhabited`, the i.i.d. resampling flow with outflow c mu on every probability space (kb 0025). The finite form (Core/Sampling) and the marked-graph wiring (Graph/Sampling) are kept as corollary-level certificates. Supersedes the 2026-09-18 B note, whose only reason was the finite narrowing. || Closed on a finite state space, 2026-09-18 (Core/Sampling, Graph/Sampling). The paper quotes the theorem from bengio2021flow, brunswic2024theory and proves nothing; ruling (iii) of 2026-09-13 put it in scope, and the proof is the library's own. Every clause is stated: F_init(S) = F_term(S); the series E(τ) = Σ_n P(τ > n) converges and is at most F*_out(S)/F_init(S) + 1; P(τ > n) → 0 and P(τ ≤ n) → 1; and P(τ ≤ n, s_τ = y) → F_term(y)/F_term(S), which is s_τ ∼ F_term read through app:notation's normalisation. The hypotheses are the paper's: non-negative F_init, F_term, F*_out, a stochastic P*, F_term ≠ 0, and pointwise flow matching. Narrowed, disclosed: (1) V is a Fintype, measures are functions and the kernel is a matrix, where the paper takes a Polish space with finite measures; the general form waits on the measure layer (kb 0006, obstruction 2), so the row is B and not A. (2) The sampler is modelled by the time-n marginals of an absorbing chain on V × Bool and not by a path measure. By absorption every event in the statement is an event of one marginal, so this loses nothing, but no trajectory measure is built. (3) At a state where F_term + F*_out = 0 the stopping probability is taken to be 1; unstopped_eq_zero_of_G_zero shows the sampler never visits such a state. The bound is proved as the domination of the occupation measure by the minimal solution, not as an equality. Parked.strict shows it can be strict (E(τ) = 1 against 41), and Parked.inhabited shows the hypotheses are met. Marked-graph form: sampler_law needs no hypothesis on s0 → s_f. sampler_termLaw adds F(s0 → s_f) = 0 to identify the law with CycleDivergence.termLaw, and discloses it. sampler_Fk certifies s_τ(F_k) ∼ δ_{x2} on the cycle 𝒞_N for every k ≥ 0. || Quoted from Bengio et al. 2021; the paper does not prove it. Formalizing it means formalizing the sampling theorem for generative flows from scratch -- a project of its own, and outside what this paper claims.

paper_findings: **Term (i) of the proof invokes `theo:negative_control`, which the paper quotes from `brunswicEGF` and does not prove** (`proofs.tex:52-64`, used at `proofs.tex:213`). Any Lean certificate of item (1) must carry it as an external hypothesis. This is not a defect -- citing is legitimate -- but it means `equ:stable_bound` is not self-contained in the way `equ:mass_floor` is, and the two are displayed side by side as if they were.

**`equ:normalization_lemma`'s first inequality does not need `a = alpha(S)`.** It holds for any `a > 0` with `b = beta(S) > 0` and `beta >= 0`; the hypothesis is consumed only by the SECOND inequality, through `|a - b| <= ||alpha - beta||_{L^1}`. The Lean splits them accordingly (`tvD_normalization` without it, `tvD_normalization_le` with it). A generalization, not a correction -- nothing in the paper is wrong, but the lemma is stated less generally than it holds.

**Step 3 is called \"two applications of Hoelder\" but the second is a plain `L^infty` bound**, and at `q = 1` the stated conjugate pair `(q, q/(q-1))` is degenerate while the display stays true trivially (`nu_B(S)^0 = 1`). The Lean case-splits at `q = 1`. Cosmetic, but a reader following the proof at `q = 1` stalls.

Items (1)-(3) hold for a Markov kernel T on a standard Borel space. That is weaker than Polish in the safe direction: every Polish space with its Borel sigma-algebra is standard Borel. The finite measure lambda is T-invariant and is `GFNBounds.Core.General.adjoint_general`'s hypothesis. `[Nonempty S]` is implied by lambda != 0 (kb 0027). nu_B is dropped because no clause uses it, so every lambda dominated by some nu_B is covered. (1) T^lambda is Mathlib's posterior, `T†lambda`, a condKernel. It is Markov and satisfies lambda (x) T^lambda = fl_*(lambda (x) T). It is lambda-a.e. unique, and the uniqueness holds among all finite kernels, not only Markov ones. (2) lambda is T^lambda-invariant. The flip identity eq:reversal_flip holds, and (T^lambda)^lambda = T lambda-a.e. (3) M^2(lambda) is `InM2`: finite, << lambda, with (dmu/dlambda).toReal in L^2. `inM2_withDensity_ofReal` and `InM2.eq_withDensity_ofReal` show it is the cone {u lambda : 0 <= u in L^2}. <mu T | nu>_lambda = <mu | nu T^lambda>_lambda holds on M^2. Both density actions preserve M^2 and contract it. d(mu T)/dlambda = T^lambda(dmu/dlambda), and conversely. 'Operator norm 1' is an `IsLeast` of the bound set, attained at lambda. M^2 is a cone, not a normed space, so no operator object is formed; this is disclosed. STRENGTHENED, proved: the function-action contraction and operator norm 1 hold on every L^p(lambda), 1 <= p <= infinity. The adjointness holds for every Hoelder pair with signed u, v, which is the form theo:first_variation_full's proof consumes. (4) The general half is items (1)-(2) at T = the loop closure, reading the balance constraint of (lambda, pi_->) as lambda (x) pi_-> = pi_<- (x) lambda, as the paper's own proof of (4) does. 'Balanced flow' is not a separate Lean object in the general setting. The finite-graph half (lambda > 0, the entrywise formula, support on the edges of the loop closure, pi_->^lambda(s_f -> s_0) = 1) is in GFNBounds/Core/Adjoint.lean: `reversal`, `reversal_hatEdge`, `reversal_snk_src`. `IsInvariant.toReal_reversal_singleton` shows the general reversal equals that finite one at every lambda-charged atom. Not formalized, and not part of the statement: the Riesz step in the proof of (3). Inhabited: `isInvariant_const` gives a non-trivial (T, lambda) on any standard Borel space. This supersedes the 2026-09-08 finite-only closure and its 2026-09-14 correction; the kernel Jensen is `lintegral_rpow_le` via eLpNorm monotonicity in the exponent (kb 0043). || CORRECTION 2026-09-14: the kernel Jensen called 'GENUINELY MISSING FROM MATHLIB' below exists at this pin -- ConvexOn.map_integral_le applied to each fibre kappa x (Analysis/Convex/Integral.lean), and ConvexOn.map_condExp_le for the conditional form; the lambda-reversal itself is ProbabilityTheory.posterior (Probability/Kernel/Posterior.lean, compProd_posterior_eq_map_swap, posterior_posterior), on a StandardBorel space. PARTIAL 2026-09-08, sorry-free, axiom-swept, graduated -- FINITE state space, disclosed. All three items on a general kernel over a Fintype with a general NON-NEGATIVE invariant lambda (not tied to a marked graph), so Balance/Lift and the DB block get a reversal layer to build on: (1) existence, Markov-ness a.e. and the characterizing identity lam x * R x y = lam y * A y x, with lambda-a.e. uniqueness; (2) lambda is invariant for the reversal, the flip identity -- the relation is SYMMETRIC, which is the whole content -- and the a.e. involution; (3) mutual adjointness on L^2(lambda), each density action is the other's function action, the contraction, and the operator norm EXACTLY 1 as an `IsLeast` with attainment at lambda. Two things came out better than the paper's phrasing, both stated as such: EXISTENCE IS UNCONDITIONAL -- the identity holds even where lambda(x) = 0, because invariance forces lambda(y)A(y->x) = 0 there, so only Markov-ness of that row degrades (`IsMarkovOn` vs `IsMarkov`); and the INVOLUTION NEEDS ONLY lambda(x) != 0, not lambda(y) != 0, since lambda(x) != 0 = lambda(y) forces A(x->y) = 0. No lambda > 0 is assumed anywhere; 'lambda-a.e.' is `lam x != 0`. `Graph.reversal`, `pdens` and `qact` are all `rfl`-equal to the general definitions, so every theorem applies to the graph objects verbatim. NOT DONE: the general Polish case. Items (1)-(2) are reachable at this Mathlib pin (`Measure.condKernel`, `eq_condKernel_of_measure_eq_compProd`, `Measure.compProd`, `Measure.fst_map_swap`); item (3) is obstruction 2 in full, and ONE PIECE IS GENUINELY MISSING FROM MATHLIB: a kernel-Jensen `(int u d kappa_x)^2 <= int u^2 d kappa_x`, which would have to be built from `inner_mul_le_norm_mul_norm` on L^2(kappa x).

statements.label: theo:first_variation_full
statements.scope_notes: CLOSED 2026-09-19 in bucket A, on a general measurable space (GFNBounds/Core/FirstVariationGeneral.lean, built on Core/AdjointGeneral.lean); audited by an agent that did not write it. `theo_first_variation_full` carries the paper's hypotheses verbatim: lem:adjoint's setting (Polish weakened in the safe direction to StandardBorelSpace, T Markov, lambda finite, invariant, non-zero), mu ~ lambda with d mu/d lambda in L^2 (InM2), mu T << mu, r essentially in [a,b] with 0 < a, nu finite with nu << mu (which d nu/d mu presupposes) and d nu/d mu in L^inf(mu), g C^1 on (0,inf) with g' locally Lipschitz, nu_G finite ~ lambda. nu_B is dropped: no clause involves it. Conclusion in seven clauses: (1) the signed measure (T^lambda - r)[psi lambda] = (psi+ lambda)T^lambda - (psi- lambda)T^lambda - r psi lambda has lambda-density T psi - r psi, setwise; (2) (d nu_G/d lambda) times it has nu_G-density T psi - r psi; (3) that density is in L^2(nu_G); (4) it represents the derivative of s -> L(mu + s delta) at 0 in <.|.>_{nu_G} for every essentially bounded d delta/d mu (a superset of the paper's class; d(delta T)/d mu in L^inf is automatic, abs_dirPush_le); (5) uniquely among L^2(nu_G) functions, testing only directions with |d delta/d mu| <= 1/2; (6) the uniform second-order remainder with an explicit constant, nu(S)(16 K b^2 + 4 M b) c^2 on |d delta/d mu| <= c, c <= 1/2, bc <= a/2, K a Lipschitz constant of g' on [a/3, 3b], M a bound of |g'| on [a,b]; (7) such K, M exist. 'The derivative is represented by' is thus certified both along lines (4) and uniformly on a ball of the admissible cone (6); no continuous linear functional on M(S) is formed, the admissible directions being a cone in a space the library does not topologize. Proved and disclosed as unused: d mu/d lambda in L^2 (the case where it fails is inhabited, e.g. T the identity kernel), mu T << mu (implied by mu ~ lambda and invariance), lambda != 0; clauses (1)-(5) need g C^1 only. psi = g'(r) d nu/d mu need not be measurable (g' only continuous on (0,inf)); every clause is stated for the paper's psi and passes through a measurable version. Hypotheses shown inhabited (theo_first_variation_full_hypotheses_inhabited: T = const pi, lambda = mu = nu = pi, a = b = 1), at a balanced base point; the conclusion concerns the unbalanced mu + s delta. The finite forms (Balance/FirstVariation.lean, Flow.lean) stay as the Fintype specialization and carry the trajectory and gradient-flow declarations other rows cite. || 2026-09-14: existence of the (log x)^2 and (x-1)^2 gradient flows on a finite ergodic chain is now proved in GFNBounds/Balance/FlowExistence.lean; the 'Existence is NOT proved in Lean' sentences below are superseded. || FLOW PREDICATE REPAIRED (2026-09-13, author-approved; independently audited). IsGradientFlow asked the ODE at every real t and had no solution from a non-balanced start for (log x)^2, so the flow theorems were vacuous; it now asks forall t >= 0 (two-sided derivative at 0; any forward solution extends linearly below 0). 17 auxiliary signatures gained a 0 <= t or lost their negative times; no paper-level statement changed. The audit found no remaining hypothesis a forward solution cannot meet, and confirmed existence of a forward solution as mathematics (local Lipschitz field on the open cone, a priori bounds from the invariant sphere, loss antitone, mass monotone and pos_of_loss_le, continuation; RK4 checks on the two-vertex swap and the five-cycle). Existence is NOT proved in Lean, and the paper assumes rather than proves it: a disclosure, not a blocker. Before the repair: THIS ROW stays partial; its flow-hypothesis declarations are vacuous and must be re-checked after the repair. || PRIOR LOG: PARTIAL 2026-09-08, sorry-free, axiom-swept, graduated -- FINITE state space, and it is the KEYSTONE: three strict-library files (Balance/MassIdentity, Balance/Lojasiewicz, Balance/Freezing) had each disclosed this as a missing dependency and treated D = Q phi - r phi as a DEFINITION. It is now a THEOREM. `hasDerivAt_loss_ipL2`: for every direction d, the directional derivative of L at mu is <lossGradDensity ... | d>_{L^2(lambda)}; and `lossGradDensity_unique`: no other function represents those derivatives. So the three disclosures collapse, and each file now carries a dated amendment pointing here. The general preconditioner nu_G = varpi.lambda is covered (`hasDerivAt_loss_ipL2_precond`), so it is NOT a restriction. The paper's own second-order expansion is transcribed verbatim (`ratio_expansion`, `remainder_abs_le`). CROSS-CHECKED NUMERICALLY, not merely proved: `twoState_hasDerivAt_loss` evaluates the theorem on prop:nonlinear_freezing(2)'s two-state chain with g = (x-1)^2 and gets 9/16, computed by hand two ways -- off the perturbed ratios and off the gradient side -- before the Lean was run. A transposed kernel or a flipped sign would have shown there. TWO RESIDUES: the state space is finite, so the general measured-space statement stays bucket D; and criticality is DIRECTIONAL rather than Frechet -- which makes `balanced_of_hasDerivAt_zero` stronger than a Frechet version, since the hypothesis is weaker. The paper's uniform-remainder route, which would give Frechet, is stated as a standalone inequality and disclosed as not carried in that form. TRAJECTORY FORM ADDED (Balance/Flow.lean): `hasDerivAt_loss_comp_ipL2` differentiates the loss along an arbitrary curve, and `hasDerivAt_loss_flow` specializes to the gradient flow. The ODE is stated COMPONENTWISE on a Fintype, so no Frechet layer, no HasFDerivAt on V -> R and no CLM construction was needed -- which is what unblocked six statements previously recorded as needing 'a gradient-flow / LaSalle layer'.

paper_findings: **Almost every hypothesis of `theo:first_variation_full` is free in the finite model**, and one is not used at all. Vacuous on a `Fintype`: `d mu/d lambda in L^2(lambda)`, `mu T << mu`, `r` essentially bounded above, `nu` finite, `d nu/d mu in L^inf(mu)`, `lambda` finite. Derived rather than assumed: `0 < r` (`ratio_pos`). Replaced by the finite-dimensional chain rule: `g'` locally Lipschitz and continuous -- only `HasDerivAt g (gd y) y` for `y > 0` is used. And **`T` is never required to be a Markov kernel**: row-stochasticity is used nowhere, only `K >= 0`, and only in the adjoint step. Invariance of `lambda` is carried but spent only inside `lem:adjoint`(3) -- the derivative formula itself holds for an arbitrary matrix. Worth knowing: it says the first-variation formula is insensitive to the chain, and everything specific to `T` enters through the reversal.

statements.scope_notes: CLOSED 2026-09-19 in bucket A, on a general standard Borel space, at the paper's specialization T = pi_<-, mu = nu = F_<-, nu_G = lambda, pi_->^lambda the lambda-reversal of pi_<- (lem:adjoint(4)); pi_<- is any Markov kernel with a finite invariant lambda ~ F_<- (the graph structure of a backward policy is not used), and the unused L^2 and Lipschitz hypotheses of the theorem are not asked. (x-1)^2 (cor_gradient_formulas_sq): pi_->^lambda lambda = lambda, pi_->^lambda(r lambda) has lambda-density pi_<- r, and the density 2(pi_<- r - 1 - r^2 + r) represents the derivative; the measure identity 2(pi_->^lambda - r)[(r-1)lambda] = 2(pi_->^lambda(r lambda) - lambda - r^2 lambda + r lambda) is the linear combination of these pieces, not stated as one equation. |x-1| (cor_gradient_formulas_abs): under the paper's repaired hypothesis, |r - 1| >= a' > 0 F-a.e., the first display holds with g'(r) replaced by sign(r - 1), proved directly (|x-1| continuous, differentiable off 1) rather than through the paper's smoothing g~; uniqueness is not restated for this case (representative_unique applies). The closing gloss (the hypothesis excludes every flow whose ratio comes arbitrarily close to 1 on a set of positive measure, the balanced flow among them) is the negation of the hypothesis read in words and carries nothing to certify. The finite forms in Balance/GradientFormulas.lean remain, with their two-state numerical cross-checks (5/16, 3/8). || PARTIAL 2026-09-08, sorry-free, axiom-swept, graduated -- a corollary of theo:first_variation_full, exactly as the paper presents it, on a FINITE state space. BOTH DISPLAYS CLOSED for g = (x-1)^2, and the |x-1| case closed on flows balanced at NO state (hne : forall x, r(x) != 1; corrected 2026-09-13 -- the excluded set is every flow balanced at even one state, the balanced flow r = 1 among them, not the balanced flow alone; on a finite space with lambda > 0 this is the paper's repaired hypothesis 'r essentially bounded away from 1'). paper_findings: **The `|x-1|` sentence of `cor:gradient_formulas` is not a corollary of the theorem above it.** `proofs.tex:497` says the case is \"analogous, with `g'(r)` replaced by the sign of `r-1`\", and `:501` that `g'(r) = eps(r)` almost everywhere. But `theo:first_variation_full` hypothesizes `g` continuously differentiable with locally Lipschitz derivative, and `|x-1|` is not differentiable at `1` -- so the corollary's third sentence does not follow from its stated premise. The Lean closes the case under `r(x) != 1` for every `x`, where the sign IS a genuine derivative and the display holds with no reinterpretation. **The restriction is not cosmetic and not removable by better tactics**: the excluded set `{r == 1}` is exactly the BALANCED FLOW (`ratio_eq_one_iff_balanced`) -- the minimiser, and the one point the surrounding theory cares about -- and near it `|r_t(x) - 1| ~ |t . rdot(x)|`, so the non-differentiability is real. The honest general form is a subgradient statement, which needs a non-smooth first variation the library does not have. Either the corollary should carry `r != 1`, or the `|x-1|` case needs its own argument.

This is the contraction of 𝓜²(λ₂), read as the paper defines it ('Four measures': non-negative measures with square-integrable density), and every such measure is finite (`isFiniteMeasure_withDensity_of_sq`). paper_findings: **The contraction step of `lem:lift_wellposed` names the wrong conditional** (`proofs.tex:521`). The proof says '*since under lambda_2 the conditional law of s given s' is pi_back(s' -> .), the map d mu/d lambda_2 |-> d(m_1 mu)/d lambda is a conditional expectation*'. Both halves are true but they are about different conditionals: averaging against `pi_back(s' -> .)` produces the SECOND marginal `m_2 mu`. The map `eq:muK2_density` actually needs is `d(m_1 mu)/d lambda (x) = sum_w (d mu/d lambda_2)(x,w) pi_forward^lambda(x -> w)` -- the conditional expectation given the FIRST coordinate, against the FORWARD conditional, which the same lemma introduces one sentence later. The conclusion is unaffected: both conditional expectations are L^2 contractions, and 'both marginals of lambda_2 equal lambda', which the paper does state, closes either route. A slip in the proof's citation, not an error in the result -- the formalization takes the forward route.

paper_findings: **APPLIED 2026-09-08 (proofs.tex:760).** The hypothesis on `m` was unsatisfiable as literally written: `m == 0` on the open `U^- u U^+` and `m > 0` elsewhere makes the zero set of a continuous function open, hence clopen in the connected `(0, +inf)`, hence everything, contradicting `m(1) = 2`. The proposition was therefore VACUOUS. Repaired to `closure(U^-) subset (0,1)`, `closure(U^+) subset (1,+inf)`, `m == 0` on the closures, `m > 0` elsewhere; 'nonempty bounded open intervals' was retained, because closure containment does NOT bound `U^+` above (`closure((2,+inf)) = [2,+inf) subset (1,+inf)`) and boundedness is consumed twice -- directly at :780 for a finite `C'`, and indirectly in item (1) where `r` band-valued must be essentially bounded to meet theo:first_variation_full's hypothesis. The proof needed no change: every step consumes only `m` in C^inf, `m >= 0`, `m` bounded, `m` continuous with `m(1) = 2`, and `m == 0` on the bands. The clause `m > 0 elsewhere` -- the one the edit weakened -- is consumed nowhere, which is what makes the weakening harmless. Both instantiations (item (2)'s bands, rem:freezing(ii)) satisfy the repaired hypothesis with margin.

**The existence claim is now POSSIBLE but still not MADE.** NOT YET APPLIED, and this is the residue of the repair rather than a new defect. `prop:nonlinear_freezing` is a 'Let m ... Then ...' statement: it asserts what follows FROM such an `m` and nowhere asserts that such an `m` exists. Before the repair the class was empty and two claims were false; after it the class is nonempty and both are true, but neither the statement nor either proof supplies the witness, so the justification chain for an EXISTENCE claim still ends at a conditional. The two claims: theo:global_dichotomy_full(2) at proofs.tex:824 ('admissible C^inf generators of this kind with g''(1)=2 EXIST', discharged at :829 by citing this proposition) and prop:nonlinear_freezing's own closing sentence at :766 ('In particular, no bound ... can hold'), an impossibility claim that needs a witness. Also now supported where it was previously vacuous: prop:no_distant_equilibrium(1)'s closing prose at :790. WHAT CLOSES IT: one clause, either a typeset witness -- `m = 2 u_- u_+ / (u_-(1) u_+(1))` with `u_pm(t) = chi(a_pm - t) + chi(t - b_pm)`, `chi(s) = e^{-1/s} 1_{s>0}`, verified at 60 digits -- or a named appeal to smooth Urysohn. THE AUTHOR'S CALL: whether 'a smooth function vanishing exactly on two disjoint compact intervals' is standard enough to invoke without typesetting the witness.

**`closure(U^-) subset (0,1)` is unambiguous only if the closure is taken in R.** NOT APPLIED, low severity. The same sentence names `R_+^*` as the ambient space (`m : R_+^* -> R_+`), and under the RELATIVE closure `U^- = (0,b)` is admissible: its closure in `(0,inf)` is `(0,b] subset (0,1)`, it is bounded, and `m == 0` on `(0,b]` is realizable -- whereupon `r` band-valued is NOT essentially bounded away from 0, which is exactly what theo:first_variation_full consumes and item (1)'s proof invokes at :772. The R-reading is plainly intended and has in-file precedent (`closure(Z^p(I))` at :180, :253), which is why this is low. Closed by writing `U^- = (a^-, b^-)` with `0 < a^- < b^- < 1` and `U^+ = (a^+, b^+)` with `1 < a^+ < b^+ < inf`, or by restating theo:first_variation_full's hypotheses in item (1) -- which is already on the register.

**`rem:freezing`(ii)'s `delta` is unquantified, and the repair narrowed what it may be.** NOT APPLIED, very low. `U^mp = (1 -+ 2 delta, 1 -+ delta)`: the OLD clause admitted `delta = 1/2` (`U^- = (0, 1/2) subset (0,1)`), the new one does not (`closure = [0, 1/2]` is not a subset of `(0,1)`). The remark's own regime is `delta -> 0`, so nothing it says is touched; the fix is 'for `0 < delta < 1/2`'.

paper_findings: **APPLIED 2026-09-08 (proofs.tex:817, both occurrences).** Claim 1's number was wrong: the expected backward-trajectory length is `3/(1-p)`, not the printed `(1+2p)/(1-p)`. `sigma_bar` is `E_{x ~ pihat(s_f -> .)} E(sigma | X_0 = x)`; the target row is the point mass at `x_3`, so `sigma_bar = E(sigma | X_0 = x_3) = 3/(1-p)`, while the printed value is `E(sigma | X_0 = x_1)` -- the MINIMUM of the four hitting times, so neither `sigma_bar` nor `sigma_*`. Verified three ways: exact rational arithmetic, 200,000-trajectory Monte-Carlo at three values of `p`, and the Lean (`sigmaBar_eq`). **And it was worse than a wrong number.** With the printed value, `prop:morozov_rate`(1) forces `lambda(x_i) = 1/3` and `lambda(s_0) = (1-p)/3`, total mass `1 + 2(1-p)/3 != 1` -- so `lambda` was not a probability measure, contradicting the proposition's own hypothesis AND the remark's own next sentence. The correction removes an internal contradiction, not just an inaccuracy.

**Claim 3's `r(s_0) ~ M(1-p)` is on the wrong convention.** On the paper's own `u := d mu / d lambda`, set two lines earlier in prop:no_distant_equilibrium, `r(s_0) = M` **exactly** -- the `(1-p)` cancels because `lambda(s_0)` already carries it. `M(1-p)` is what the *counting*-measure reading gives, and on that reading `r(x_3) = p + 1/M` rather than `p + (1-p)/M`. Both readings are certified in the Lean. Since the remark writes `~` and both give `r(s_0)` linear in `M`, this is a notational slip and not an error -- but the two readings are not interchangeable.

**Claim 4's transient is `Theta(M^2)`, not `O(M/log M)`** -- wrong by `Theta(M log M)`, and in the optimistic direction. NOT YET APPLIED. The remark names the force as `|g'(r) r| = 2 log r(s_0)` but drops the `d nu / d mu = w/u` factor, which equals 1 only at `t = 0`: at `p = 1/2, M = 100` the speed is `9.2103 = 2 log M` at `u(s_0) = 1` and `0.0277` at `u(s_0) = 50`. Dividing a deficit of order `M` by the INITIAL speed is what produces `M/log M`. A one-line argument using what `prop:no_distant_equilibrium`'s own proof already uses (proofs.tex:813, 'changes the gradient field by the factor 1/m'): the field is homogeneous of degree -1, so the trajectory from `c u_0` runs at speed `c^{-2}`; with `||u_0|| = Theta(M)` and a finite transient for the normalized shape, that is `Theta(M^2)`. Measured `T/M^2` = 0.72003, 0.72025, 0.72018, 0.72015, 0.72013, 0.72013 for `M` = 10..320 (fitted exponent 2.0000); `T log M / M^2` is not constant, so there is no `1/log M` either. **The paper's own certified bound already says so**: proofs.tex:813's `L(mu_0)/c(delta)^2 ~ ||u_0||^2 L(mu_0)` scales as `M^2 log^2 M`, so the remark claims a transient SMALLER than the proposition it illustrates guarantees. Second location, also wrong and not even agreeing with the remark it cites: `proofs.tex:381`, 'a transient linear in the overload'.

**The closing sentence's 'every rate degenerates' is true only of the CERTIFIED rates.** `rho = g''(1) w_min / B-hat^2 ~ w_min (1-p)^2/2 -> 0` and `kappa ~ lambda_min^{1/2} -> 0`, so as a statement about what the theorems guarantee it is right as written. But the ACTUAL local exponential rate does not degenerate: the true coercivity constant `||sum_n (P^n - Pi)||` rises only to the golden ratio (1.10535, 1.48383, 1.60367, 1.61659, 1.61789, 1.61802 at `p` = 0.5 ... 0.99999), giving `>= 0.7639 w_min` uniformly in `p` against a certified `5e-11 w_min` at `p = 0.99999` -- six orders of magnitude. Note also that `B-hat` blows up at the OTHER endpoint too (722.8 at `p` = 0.01), where the narrative suggests nothing. Costs one line to dismiss; worth dismissing explicitly, because the sentence invites the reading that convergence itself stalls, which is false. Related: the clause is true under `lem:sigma_mixing`'s `B-hat = sum_n beta-hat_n` (sum of norms) but NOT under the headline's `||sum_n (P^n - Pi)||` (norm of the sum), which saturates at 1.618 here -- a pre-existing definitional matter worth one look.

**The range of `p` is never stated.** The example needs `p` in `(0,1)`: at `p = 1` the backward policy is not positive on `s_0 -> x_1` and the chain is reducible; at `p = 0` not positive on `x_3 -> x_1`. Either way `prop:morozov_rate`'s hypothesis 'a backward policy positive on its edges' fails and the chain becomes periodic, so `B-hat = +inf`.

paper_findings: **`N(s_0) = N(s_f) = 1` is stated in the paper as a *convention* (`proofs.tex:840`, 'with the convention N(s_0) = N(s_f) = 1') but comes out as a THEOREM.** Once `N` is characterized as the killed occupation measure of one excursion, both values are forced. **The proof of item (2) transfers coercivity from `I - Q` to `I - P` by 'their restricted inverses have the same norm'** (`proofs.tex:870`), which is an operator-adjoint argument. On a finite space it has a shorter route that is NOT available on this proof's construction: the duality pairing `<h,h> = <h,(I-Q)w> = <(I-P)h,w> <= ||(I-P)h|| ||w||` gives the same conclusion in two lines using only pointwise adjointness. Worth a footnote if the appendix ever wants to be self-contained at the finite level.

**2026-09-13, `proof-checker`.** The adjoint transfer step is CORRECT: both `P` and `Q` preserve the mean-zero subspace by invariance of `lambda`, item (2)'s own coercivity makes `(I-Q)` injective hence invertible there in finite dimension, `(I-P)` restricted is its adjoint, and the inverse of an adjoint is the adjoint of the inverse. The Lean declined the operator-norm layer, not the argument. The duality two-liner needs `w` with `(I-Q)w = h - Pi h`; the proof's `u` solves `(I-Q)u = (I-Q)h` and is then consumed by the harmonicity step, so the shorter route means re-running the construction at a different input and deleting two steps -- a restructuring of a certified proof. NOT a detour within the printed argument.

paper_findings: **`rem:loop_closure_necessary` is one reading away from being false, and the reading it needs is not stated.** The remark's proof turns on 'summing over v gives `f_out(u) = sum_v f_out(v) pi_back(v->u)`', which silently requires `pi_forward(u -> .)` to be a probability row at EVERY state u -- including s_f. On the loop closure that is automatic (every vertex has an out-edge), but the remark is explicitly about G *without* the wrap edge, where s_f has no outgoing edge at all and so carries no row. Under the symmetric reading -- `pi_forward` undefined at s_f, just as `pi_back` is undefined at s_0 -- the remark FAILS. Counterexample, checked by hand and against the Lean definition: G = (s_0 -> s_f), `pi_back(s_f -> s_0) = 1`, `pi_forward(s_0 -> s_f) = 1`, `pi_forward(s_f -> .) = 0`. Then every constant `f_out(s_0) = f_out(s_f) = c` satisfies the constraint `f_out(u) pi_forward(u->v) = pi_back(v->u) f_out(v)` at all four pairs, so the frozen-backward family is a RAY, not {0}. The row sum of `pi_forward` at s_f is 0, not 1, which is exactly where the marginal argument breaks. Nothing in item (2) of `theo:universality_graphs` is affected -- that is stated on the loop closure. But the remark as written could use a clause fixing the convention at s_f.

paper_findings: **The parenthetical `M = max_x p_F(s_o -> x) = 3/8` in the proof of item (ii) (`silva_comparison.tex:95`) needs `K >= 2`.** At `K = 1` the filler weight `1/(2K) = 1/2` is the largest forward probability, so `M = 1/2`. This does not touch the proposition: what the statement claims is `M' <= 1`, and that holds for every `K >= 1`. Found while formalizing `star_Mprime`; the Lean carries the correct value at every `K`.

**The final clause leaves a monotonicity hypothesis implicit** (`silva_comparison.tex:86`): \"no bound `TV <= F(E, chi^2, M')` with `F` independent of the state space and `F(E, 0, 1) -> 0` as `E -> 0` can hold\". The witness family has `M' = 3/8`, not `1`, so `F(E, 0, 1) -> 0` alone does not contradict it unless `F` is non-decreasing in its third argument. The Lean `no_three_argument_bound` therefore feeds `F`'s third slot any `c` with `M' <= c` (so in particular `c = 1`), which is the reading the paper means; the literal reading needs the monotonicity said out loud. A companion `no_state_space_free_bound` avoids the question by quantifying only over `F : R -> R`.

paper_findings: **The prose conclusion is refuted; the propositions stand.** In the exact setting of `prop:blur_vs_drop` (minimal-loss flow, uniform ν_T), overshoot blurs at a cost ((z−t)/z)·TV(unif‖κ/t), while undershoot past the water level drops only the target mass below it. For a peaked target the drop is cheaper: 10 states, 97% of κ on one — once the level passes the low states, κ̂ is a point mass, the sampler can stop only there, and TV = 0.030 for every s in [0.05, 0.7], against 0.041–0.358 for overshoot (recomputed independently). Below the threshold (s = 0.02) overshoot is marginally better (0.0171 vs 0.0178). A random sweep of 1,500 ergodic chains found undershoot better in 373/375 cases with Dirichlet(0.1) targets and 5/375 with Dirichlet(3). `prop:overshoot` is about the certificate and stands; the sentences crediting the sampled law with the same preference do not. paper_findings: **Overreach.** `app_replay.tex:237–247` (proof `:260–262`) presents J_T(α) = K(ν_B(𝒮)/α)^{1/q}e^{−c(1−α)T} as the certified error, with K 'collecting the T- and α-independent factors'. The chain through theo:training_speed_full does not give that: the entry time t₁ ≤ T₀(ν_α) has w_min²ε₀⁴ in its denominator, the local rate carries a trajectory-dependent m₁, and ‖w(ν_α)‖∞ and L_{g,ν_α}(μ₀) depend on α. With ν_B carried by the internal states, w_min(ν_α) = 1 − α exactly (at s₀ and s_f), so at α = 1 — where α* sits for small T — the theorem certifies nothing. Using the transfer lemma at q = 2 inside a general-q envelope needs q ≤ 2. Strongest supported form: for q ∈ [1, 2] and α ≤ α_max < 1, TV_T ≤ K(α_max)(ν_B(𝒮)/α)^{1/q}e^{−c(1−α)T}, minimized at min(α_max, 1/(qcT)). The audit's family is λ mixed with `ones(n)/n` over all vertices, s₀ and s_f included, which is also what Figure A3's caption prints ('unif'); per the review, 'the exact-rate optimum can sit at α = 1' holds for that family (13/40 graphs) and for none of the stated one (0/40). (Read-only review of Appendices C–F, 2026-09-24; not yet re-checked by `proof-checker`.)

paper_findings: **Conditional as proved; the rest is unproved.** The Young/Grönwall step is correct as a conditional statement. Adding variables adds gradient terms only under a product metric, unstated. In (F, P_B) the constant becomes ≥ ϱ_σ/m² (Euclidean F, m = Z(2+σ̄)) or ≈ λ_min·ϱ_σ (log F). ϱ_min > 0 fails as the drift nears its target (`prop:constants_path`). The argument is deterministic, not stochastic approximation. On slow time scales Tikhonov gives trajectory error O(λ_reg); O(λ_reg²) is the vector-field error (reasoned in the review, not tested). (Read-only review of Appendices C–F, 2026-09-24; not yet re-checked by `proof-checker`.)

**PointwiseInv.lean**

## SCOPE (disclosed)

* Stated for `cap = none` only. On the truncation the incoming edges differ at the cap
  (`lem:doubling_truncation_irreducible`), and `GFNBounds.Doubling.TruncationStat` already
  constructs `Stat S (some K)` by finite linear algebra, so no truncated version is needed here.
* The equation at the source is not separate: `s₀ = lad 0`, and `hpt` at `k = 0` is the balance
  there. What is separate is `hsink`, `μ(s_f) = μ(s₀)`, the sink having the single incoming edge
  `s₀ → s_f`.
* Non-negativity of `μ` is used only for the domination bounds that give summability of the two
  flux series; no positivity is needed and none is concluded.

## Hypothesis checklist

| what the equivalence needs | here |
|---|---|
| `μ ≥ 0` | ✓ carried (`hnn`) |
| `μ` summable along the ladder | ✓ carried (`hsum`); summability on `St` follows |
| `μT = μ` at every state | ✓ carried as `hsink` and `hpt` |
| `f` bounded | ✓ carried, exactly as `Stat.inv` states it |
| normalisation `Σμ = 1` | ⚠ weakened: not needed, and not assumed |

**Setting.lean**

## SCOPE (disclosed)

This file is definitions only; it asserts no mathematics. Two things it deliberately does **not**
model. First, the *density* action `P` of `def:doubling_setting` is not defined here — only the
function action `P⋆`; `P` is `Stat.dens` in `Adjoint.lean`, and the adjoint identity `P⋆ = P*`
on `L²(λ)` of `lem:adjoint`(3) is `Stat.adjoint_pstarL2` in `AdjointL2.lean`. Second, `Stat`
carries positivity of `λ` as a **field** rather than deriving
it: `lem:doubling_irreducible` and `lem:doubling_truncation_irreducible` supply it, but every
downstream statement of the appendix quantifies over "an invariant probability", so positivity
belongs in the hypothesis and not in a global theorem.

Note that `Stat` is *not* the hypothesis of the decay results. `prop:doubling_cut`,
`theo:doubling_decay` and `theo:doubling_sharp` are stated for an arbitrary positive real sequence
satisfying the cut-balance recursion — no invariance, no normalisation, no positive recurrence —
and `cor:doubling_truncation` Step 4 relies on that, feeding them `λ^K` extended past the cap by
`1`. See `GFNBounds.Doubling.CutBalance` for the predicate those results actually use.

statements.label: lem:doubling_fixed_points
statements.title: the fixed points of the function action are the constants
statements.scope_notes:
Disclosed by the modules themselves; no note curated against the statement yet.

**FixedPoints.lean**

## SCOPE (disclosed)

⚠ **weakened hypothesis, and a narrowed statement.** Two departures, both on the face of the
Lean statement:

* `L²(λ)` is replaced by **bounded** functions. Boundedness is what makes `Stat.inv` applicable
  to `f²` without an integrability side condition, and every consumer in this library tests
  against bounded functions. A bounded function on a probability space is in `L²`, so this is a
  sub-case of the paper's, not a generalization.
* Only the `P⋆` half is proved *in this file*. Both halves at the paper's hypothesis
  `f ∈ L²(λ)` are `Stat.ker_eq_const` in `FixedPointsP.lean`, with the density action `P`
  modelled as `Stat.dens` (`Adjoint.lean`); this file stays as the elementary route.

The proof is the paper's: Jensen for the one-step law and the strictly convex `t ↦ t²` gives
`(P⋆f)² ≤ P⋆(f²)` pointwise, invariance makes the `λ`-integral of the gap vanish, positivity of
`λ` makes the gap vanish at every state of the chain, and equality in Jensen at a doubling state
forces `f(2m) = f(m−1)`. Constancy then follows along the ladder without ever using the target
row, since the decrement alone connects it.

## Hypothesis checklist

| paper hypothesis | here |
|---|---|
| irreducible kernel | ✓ implied: the ladder is connected by the decrement alone |
| invariant probability positive at every state | ✓ carried (`Stat`, positivity on chain) |
| `f ∈ L²(λ)` with `P⋆f = f` | ⚠ narrowed to bounded `f` |
| conclusion `= ℝ·1` | ✓ carried, as `f x = f s₀` at every state of the chain |

**FixedPointsP.lean**

## SCOPE (disclosed)

* **The fixed-point equation is required on the chain**, i.e. `λ`-a.e., which is what membership
  of `L²(λ)` — a space of classes — makes available, and the conclusion is likewise `u = u(s₀)` on
  the chain. On the loop closure `OnChain` is vacuous and both are pointwise statements.
* **`u ∈ L²(λ)` is carried**, as the paper states it. It is used exactly once: to make the total
  Jensen gap a convergent sum, so that a sum of non-negative terms vanishing forces each term to.
* **`RowOnChain` is carried**, as everywhere in this layer (`LpLayer`, SCOPE).
* The statement is about `ker(Id − P)` **as a set of `λ`-classes on this graph**; the paper's
  `= ℝ·1` is rendered as "constant on the chain", the two being the same statement in `L²(λ)`.

## Hypothesis checklist

| paper hypothesis | here |
|---|---|
| `T` irreducible | ⚠ **not assumed**; the climbing edge of `T̂` is exhibited instead, which is stronger information about this graph and weaker as a hypothesis |
| `λ` invariant probability, positive at every state | ✓ carried (`Stat`; positivity on the chain) |
| `u ∈ L²(λ)` | ✓ carried |
| `Pu = u` | ✓ carried, on the chain (`λ`-a.e.) |
| — | ⚠ **added**: `RowOnChain S cap` |

**LpLayer.lean**

## SCOPE (disclosed)

The file is definitions plus the dictionary. It settles **no** statement of the appendix in
full; the one statement it advances is `lem:doubling_fixed_points`, whose `P⋆` half it upgrades
from bounded `f` to `f ∈ L²(λ)`; the `P` half is `FixedPointsP.lean`.

* **`P⋆` on `L²` is here; its adjoint `P` is in `Adjoint.lean` / `AdjointL2.lean`.** `pstarL2`
  is built as a contraction of `L²(μ)`, which is the `p = 2` case of `lem:doubling_operator`(1)'s
  first clause. The second clause — `P⋆ = P*` — is `Stat.adjoint_pstarL2` (`AdjointL2.lean`),
  with `P` modelled as `Stat.dens` / `Stat.densL2`; this file does not claim it.
* **The contraction is proved at `p = 2` only in this file.** The pointwise Jensen step available
  here is `sq_pstar_le` (`FixedPoints.lean`), which is the square; the general `p ∈ [1,∞]` case
  is `Stat.eLpNorm_pstar_le_of_memLp` (`LpContraction.lean`). `Stat.eLpNorm_two_pstar_le` is
  therefore stated at `2`.
* **`fixed_const_memLp` states the fixed-point equation on the chain, i.e. `λ`-a.e.**, which is
  weaker than the paper's pointwise `P⋆f = f` and is what `prop:doubling_unsolvable` (working in
  `L²(λ)`, a space of classes) actually has. The conclusion is likewise `f = f(s₀)` on the chain,
  i.e. `f = f(s₀)` in `L²(λ)`, which is `ker(Id − P⋆) ∩ L²(λ) = ℝ·1`. The `P` half of
  `eq:doubling_fixed` is `Stat.ker_eq_const` (`FixedPointsP.lean`).
* **The `L²` operator carries one hypothesis the paper does not name: `RowOnChain`.** On the
  truncation at `K`, `pstar` at the sink reads the target row at `1, …, d`, and if `K < d` those
  states are off-chain — where `λ` vanishes and a.e. equality says nothing — so `pstar` would not
  descend to `λ`-classes. `RowOnChain S cap` is `d ≤ K`, automatic on the loop closure
  (`rowOnChain_none`), and `cor:doubling_truncation` takes `K ≥ d` throughout. This is a genuine
  hypothesis of the construction, not of the mathematics, and it is on the face of the statement.

## Hypothesis checklist

| paper hypothesis | here |
|---|---|
| invariant probability `λ` positive at every state | ✓ carried (`Stat`; positivity on chain) |
| the state space is countable | ✓ carried (`St` is `Countable`, `Setting.lean`; discrete σ-algebra) |
| `p ∈ [1,∞)` for the norm identification | ✓ carried (`hp0`, `hpt`) |
| `p ∈ [1,∞]` for the contraction | `p = 2` here; every `p ∈ [1,∞]` in `LpContraction.lean` |
| `P⋆ = P*` on `L²(λ)` | not claimed here; `Stat.adjoint_pstarL2` in `AdjointL2.lean` |
| `f ∈ L²(λ)` with `P⋆f = f` (`lem:doubling_fixed_points`) | ✓ carried, at `L²` and a.e. |
| irreducibility (`lem:doubling_fixed_points`) | ✓ implied: the ladder is connected by the decrement alone |

**Adjoint.lean**

## SCOPE (disclosed)

* **`P` is defined by its closed form, not by a Radon–Nikodym derivative.** The paper's
  `d((uλ)T)/dλ` is characterised by `∫v d((uλ)T) = ⟨Pu,v⟩_λ` at every bounded `v`; that is
  `Stat.tsum_dens_mul` read with `Balance.tsum_mact`, and it pins `Pu` at every state of the
  chain, `λ` being positive there. No Riesz representation theorem is used, and none is needed:
  the space is a weighted sequence space.
* **The identity is on the plain-real layer**, `∑' x, λ(x)·(Pu)(x)·v(x) = ∑' x, λ(x)·u(x)·(P⋆v)(x)`.
  Its transcription into `⟪·,·⟫` on `MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 μ` needs the Bochner-integral half of the
  `LpLayer` dictionary; so `ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint (pstarL2) = densL2` is **not** claimed
  here, and neither is `‖P⋆^n − Π‖ = β̂_n`, which is its corollary — both are proved in
  `AdjointL2.lean` (`Stat.adjoint_pstarL2`, `Stat.norm_pstarL2_pow_sub_piL2`).
* **`RowOnChain` is carried**, as everywhere in this layer: off the chain the transported measure
  must vanish for `Pu := (uλ)T/λ` to be the honest quotient, and at the sink that is exactly
  `d ≤ K` (`LpLayer`, SCOPE).

## Hypothesis checklist

| paper hypothesis | here |
|---|---|
| `T` Markov with invariant probability `λ` | ✓ carried (`Stat`) |
| `λ` positive at every state | ✓ carried on the chain (`Stat.pos`), which is where `P` divides |
| `u, v ∈ L²(λ)` | ✓ carried in `tsum_dens_mul_sq`; ⚠ `v` bounded in `tsum_dens_mul` |
| Fubini for `T(x,dy)λ(dx)` | ✓ replaced by `Balance.hasSum_mact`, a rearrangement of four series |
| Riesz representation | ⚠ **not used** — `P` is exhibited, not extracted |
| — | ⚠ **added**: `RowOnChain S cap` |

(1) P⋆ = funActLp, the function action ∫ v dT(x,·) on L^p(λ), a contraction for every p ∈ [1, ∞] (∞ included); P⋆ = P* and P = P⋆* on L²(λ), where P = Core.densityActionL2 is d((uλ)T)/dλ (Core.Kernel, signed densities split into parts); ‖P⋆ⁿ − Π‖ = β̂ₙ with β̂ₙ defined on P as the paper does. statements.label: lem:doubling_escape
statements.title: the descent halves at a uniform rate
statements.scope_notes:
Disclosed by the modules themselves; no note curated against the statement yet.

**Escape.lean**

## SCOPE (disclosed)

**Only Step 1 is in this file** — `eq:doubling_escape`, the analytic half. Step 2's three
sojourn bounds, `eq:doubling_sojourn`, are statements about the law of an exit time; they are
proved in `Sojourn.lean`, which models that law by the survival recursion `Decay.surv` and takes
`Decay.escape` below as its only input. Nothing here depends on that file.

Step 1 is stated here without a chain, exactly as the transition law of `lem:doubling_descent`
defines it: `P(Y₁ = j | Y₀ = y) = w_y(j)/R₀(y)` for `j ∈ W(y)`, so

  `P(Y₁ ≤ y/√2 | Y₀ = y)  =  (Σ_{j ∈ W(y), j ≤ y/√2} w_y(j)) / R₀(y)`,

and that quotient is what `Decay.escape` bounds below by `γ`. `Decay.escape_sum` is the
un-normalised half, `Σ_{j=⌈y/2⌉}^{⌊y/√2⌋} w_y(j) ≥ 2γ − 4cτ/y`, which is the paper's display.

**The threshold is explicit.** The paper's `ℓ₂` is non-effective, inheriting `c₄` and `ℓ₁` from
`lem:doubling_descent`. With `R0Bound.lean`'s effective `c₄ = 16cτ` the three requirements the
paper imposes on `ℓ₂` — that `y ≥ 2ℓ₂` force `⌈y/2⌉ ≤ ⌊y/√2⌋ ≤ y−1`, `4cτ/y ≤ γ/2` and
`c₄/y ≤ ½` — all follow from the single condition

  `y ≥ 32 c τ`,

because `cτ = p_* + c > 1` and `γ > ¼`. So `ℓ₂ := max(d+1, ⌈16cτ⌉)` works, and the paper's
conjunct `ℓ₂ ≥ 2ℓ₁` is not needed at all: at `ℓ ≥ ℓ₂` every `y ≥ 2ℓ` has `y ≥ 32cτ`, which is
where `R0_between` gives `½ ≤ R₀(y) ≤ 2`, and nothing else of `ℓ₁` is consumed. (With
`ℓ₁ = max(d+1, 32cτ)` as in `R0Bound.lean`, `ℓ₂` is in general *smaller* than `ℓ₁`.) That is
`Decay.ell2` and `Decay.escape_of_level`.

**No integral.** The paper's Step 1 compares `Σ (j+1)^{−p−1}` with `∫ t^{−p−1} dt`. Here
`sum_shift_ge` does the same comparison by telescoping against `t ↦ (t+1)^{−p}`, in the manner of
`WindowSum.lean`; the resulting bound `((a+1)^{−p} − (b+2)^{−p})/p` is the paper's, term for term.

| `s = 1` | ✓ carried, as the shape of `Decay.eps` |
| `0 < c < 1` | ✓ carried (`Decay.c_pos`, `Decay.c_lt_one`) |
| `p = p_*` the Cramér root, `τ = 2^{p_*}` | ✓ carried (`Decay.root`, `Decay.tau`) |
| `ℓ₁` of `lem:doubling_descent` | ⚠ replaced by the effective `y ≥ 32cτ`; strictly weaker, since `ℓ₁ ≥ 32cτ` there |
| `ℓ ≥ ℓ₂` and `y ≥ 2ℓ` | ✓ carried, in `escape_of_level`; `escape` takes the sharper `32cτ ≤ y` |
| `γ = √τ/(2(√τ+1))`, `0 < γ < ½` | ✓ carried (`Decay.gam`, `gam_pos`, `gam_lt_half`) |
| `c₅ = 6/γ²` and `eq:doubling_sojourn` | ✗ not proved — Step 2, see SCOPE |

The identity is asserted **on the chain** (`OnChain cap x`), which on the loop closure is every
state and on the truncation at `K` is the `K + 2` states `{s₀, 1, …, K, s_f}`. It genuinely fails
off the chain: at `x = lad (K+1)` with `m ≤ K` the left side is `−1` and the right side is `0`.

  `Stat.no_bounded_inverse`: no real `B` bounds `mass p f ≤ B · mass p ((Id−P⋆)f)` over the
  bounded mean-zero `f`. That is the inequality the paper's Step 3 actually uses, and it is what
  makes the conclusion independent of the `Lp` layer.
* The `p = 2` clauses — no bounded `S` on `L²(λ)`, the series `Σ(P⋆ⁿ − Π)` has no operator-norm
  limit, `Σ β̂_n = +∞` — are `UnboundedL2.lean` (`Stat.no_diffusionOp`,
  `Stat.not_tendsto_partialSum`, `Stat.not_summable_betaHat`), through `RayleighBridge.lean`.

statements.label: lem:doubling_ramp
statements.title: the clipped ramp
statements.scope_notes:
Disclosed by the modules themselves; no note curated against the statement yet.

**Ramp.lean**

## SCOPE (disclosed)

`L^∞(λ)` is not built. Since `λ` is positive at every state of the loop closure
(`lem:doubling_irreducible`), the `L^∞(λ)` norm *is* the supremum over states, and the two
inequalities of `eq:doubling_ramp` are stated in the two forms that supremum consumes: a pointwise
upper bound `∀ x, |·| ≤ max(1,γ,j̄)` for the defect, and an attained lower bound `∃ x, N/2 ≤ |·|`
for the function. `no_bounded_inverse_infty` is then phrased against any `B` bounding an attained
lower bound of `‖f‖` by a uniform upper bound of `‖(Id−P⋆)f‖`, **over the bounded mean-zero
`f`**, which is exactly what `‖f‖_∞ ≤ ‖S‖ ‖(Id−P⋆)f‖_∞` supplies for `f ∈ L^∞(λ)`. The
boundedness hypothesis on `f` is load-bearing: without it the statement is satisfied trivially by
the unclipped height `V`, whose defect is bounded by `max(1,γ,j̄)` while `V` itself is unbounded,
and says nothing about `L^∞(λ)`. (The 2026-09-07 morning version lacked it and was repaired the
same evening.) Nothing here depends on the `Lp` layer.

statements.title: an L^2 pair with no exact L^2 outflow
statements.scope_notes:
Disclosed by the modules themselves; no note curated against the statement yet.

**Unsolvable.lean**

## SCOPE (disclosed)

* **This refutes exact `L²` flow matching, not weak universality.** Item (1) delivers a *dense*
  range, so the conclusion of `theo:universality_L2` — a defect infimum of zero — is not
  contradicted, and whether weak universality fails on the infinite chain stays open. The
  appendix flags this itself and this file does not go past it.
* **The witness pair of item (2) is non-explicit**, by construction: `ψ` is produced by the open
  mapping argument and only known to lie outside a proper subspace, so the Lean statement is an
  `∃` and nothing here computes `f_init` or `f_term`.
* **The adjoint is not used, and `lem:doubling_operator`(1) is not assumed.** The paper argues
  that `A` has dense range from `ker A* = 0`, using `P⋆ = P*` and the `P` half of
  `lem:doubling_fixed_points`; neither is available here, `P` not being modelled
  (`LpLayer.lean`, SCOPE). The same content is delivered by `fixed_of_mem_orthogonal_range`,
  which needs only that `P⋆` is a contraction — the `p = 2` clause of `lem:doubling_operator`(1),
  proved in `LpLayer.lean` as `Stat.norm_pstarL2_le`. Nothing in this file is conditional.
* **`ker Π` is `(ℝ·1)ᗮ`**, and `Stat.mem_kerPi_iff` is the identification with the classes of
  zero `λ`-mean, which is what `Π` means. Density is stated in the ambient `L²(μ)` as
  `Submodule.topologicalClosure (Id − P⋆)L² = ker Π` rather than inside `ker Π` as a subtype;
  the two say the same thing, `ker Π` being closed.
* **`L²(λ)` is a space of classes**, so item (2)'s equation is stated `λ`-a.e. On the loop
  closure `λ` is positive at every state, so a.e. equality *is* equality (`Stat.ae_iff_eq`) and
  the a.e. reading — which is the `L²(λ)` reading, and the stronger non-existence statement — is
  the same as the pointwise one.
* The chain is the loop closure (`cap = none`), as in the paper; the `RowOnChain` hypothesis that
  `LpLayer.lean`'s `L²` operator carries is then vacuous (`rowOnChain_none`).
